content:
A revised worldview leaves a policy debt
Retracting a premise about technological benevolence should reopen policies that depended on it. The remaining rejection of regulation needs its own analysis of benefits, costs, incentives and institutional alternatives. Personal intellectual progress does not discharge that policy argument.

quote: afterward he still wanted to charge in
content:
An unchanged action need not indicate a failed update
Different models can recommend the same act, especially when the available choices are coarse. Evidence can therefore alter a rational person’s beliefs substantially without changing today’s policy. To diagnose motivated resistance, trace which premises the policy depends on and compare the recomputed alternatives; sameness alone is insufficient.

quote: far more efficient to admit one huge mistake
content:
Recheck dependencies rather than worship a dramatic reversal
A central error may require extensive reconstruction, and the willingness to do that survives. Other beliefs can remain supported by independent evidence. The size and drama of a reversal are poor measures of its accuracy; revise the actual dependency structure, not an imagined minimum amount of repentance.
